entries.reason: All four tasks show on one class page: package tree with counts plus search to find the class; a Field/Label/Type/Required/Draws-from table; extends badge, Extended-by and Lists-referenced boxes; and a Source line naming module Person and ihris-suite-4.3.3. The visualiser is a navbar tile, as the intent's 'Where' says.
At 1280 the sidebar tree, breadcrumb and five-column table are easy to scan, and each list in 'Draws from' is a link. The two relationship boxes leave some empty space, but nothing blocks the task.

At 390 the table becomes labelled cards with no overflow, and the Menu button is at least 44px tall. Relationships and Source follow in reading order. The opened-menu state (package tree and visualiser tile) is not drawn, so finding a class by package on a phone is assumed, not shown.

Required status is carried by the text yes/no as well as bold, and the linear reading order is clean (h1 > Fields > relationships > Source). But the search is a div with role=search and no input or label, nav items are not links, and the tile is a div with role=link/tabindex instead of an <a>. On mobile the table is set to display:block with ::before labels, which can strip table semantics for screen readers.
A differs from B on the axis the intent names (visualiser on a separate tile page vs on the class page). But A's visualiser page is never drawn, so that half of the comparison cannot be judged.

Fields, relationships and source are all present, and the neighbourhood graph shows extends, extended-by and list edges well. But finding a class by package stops at four package links with no in-package class list drawn. The visualiser sits on the class page and no navbar/board tile is shown, which the intent's 'Where' asks for.

The split view lets you read the graph and the field list side by side, and the legend explains box/pill and solid/dashed. At 1280 'required' sits far right, away from its label, and the lower half of the graph pane is empty. Both are layout polish, not blockers.

Swapping the graph for Extends/Extended by/Lists referenced disclosures (44px summaries, counts, the field behind each list) works well on touch. But field rows break into three uneven lines: code and right-aligned label, then 'required' alone, then the type. That is harder to scan than A's cards. Package links are hidden behind a Menu whose open state is not drawn.

The SVG has role=img with a full text alternative, and edges are told apart by dash pattern, not colour. On web, 'Select a node' has no keyboard path (the rels list is display:none above 700px), and the filter chips are spans with no button role or pressed state. Field rows are unlabelled divs, and in linear reading the visualiser h2 comes before the class h1, which strains the just-the-docs linear-reading floor.

B draws its distinguishing idea at both widths (graph beside detail on web, relationships list on phone), so it is a real alternative to A, not a restyle. Both use the same class, palette and search, so the comparison isolates the visualiser placement.

notes.A: Strengths: the most complete answer to the four tasks, and the most linear and just-the-docs-native. Its mobile card view is the clearer of the two field presentations. Most important change: draw the visualiser tile page (and the opened mobile menu) so the design can be compared to B on the visualiser. Also use real <a>/<input> elements for the nav, tile and search.
notes.B: Strengths: the relationships are much easier to grasp in the graph, and the mobile relationships list, which shows which field draws each list, is better than A's relationship boxes. Most important changes: put the class heading first in reading order (or make the graph a following section), give the graph a keyboard/list equivalent on web, add an in-package class list, and show the navbar tile the intent requires. A hybrid (A's page structure plus B's neighbourhood graph or relationships list as a section) looks worth considering.

factualIssues.issue: I2CE_Form is shown as an extends target (a badge in A; a 'form class' box in B, where the legend reads 'Box: form class'). No I2CE_Form record exists in src/*/data-model/4.3.3; it is the base class that 72 extracted records extend. A link or node for it would lead to a page that does not exist. Mark it as a base or external class.

The package counts 12/93/26/25 are records and sum to 156. A's tile says '153 classes' because iHRIS_DisciplinaryAction, iHRIS_Registration and iHRIS_SalaryGrade each appear in two packages. Both numbers are correct, but neither candidate explains the difference.

The sidebar excerpt under ihris-common (Education, Job, Person, PersonID, PersonLanguage, '... 88 more') is a sample, not the alphabetical neighbours. For example, iHRIS_PersonCompetency falls between iHRIS_Person and iHRIS_PersonID. Fine for a wireframe, but it reads like a contiguous list.

verified: Against src/ihris-common/data-model/4.3.3/iHRIS_Person.json and the rest of src/*/data-model/4.3.3: the six fields with their labels (surname_ignore has a null label), types, required flags and references; extends I2CE_Form; form 'person'; definedIn ihris-common/module/Person; extended by iHRIS_ManagePerson (only field: password) and iHRIS_QualifyPerson (only field: home); 156 records and 153 distinct classes; county and district are tied as the most-referenced lists at 7 fields each; uploads/ihris-suite-4.3.3/manifest.json has md5MatchesUpstream true. All match.
